title: What is known about 1RB1LC_1LC0RD_0LE1LA_0RF1RA_1LA0LA_---0RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_1LC0RD_0LE1LA_0RF1RA_1LA0LA_---0RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At the moments the head, in A, extends the tape to the right, the tape is two long blocks of 1s separated by 000, with a short tail 0 1; the right end moves 2 cells per such moment. A single 0 crawls through a block one cell per 5 steps (proved in Lean); with it the machine moves a quarter of the right block into the left block per round while the right block's length is ≡ 0 or 2 mod 4 (1400, 4198 → 2452, 3148 → 3240, 2361), and reshuffles both blocks when it is odd. That is a Collatz-like rule (multiply by 3/4, branch on the residue mod 4); no exact formula is written down yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 14,386 cells have been visited and 14,380 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.535). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.124).

claims.title: The crawl
claims.text: L 1 1 1 0 C> 1^(n+2) R becomes L 1^(n+4) 0 1 A> R in 5n+4 steps, for every n and any tapes L, R: one 0 crawls right through a block of 1s, one cell per 5 steps; and the same crawl as a shift rule in A. Generated by py/rules.py.

claims.title: A quarter moves per round
claims.text: At the 76 moments in the first 4·108 steps when the head, in A, extends the tape to the right, the tape is 1^x [0 1] 0 0 0 1^y 0 1 A> (up to a few marks). When y ≡ 0 or 2 (mod 4) the next such moment has y' = y − ⌈y/4⌉ and x grows by about the same amount (4198 → 3148 → 2361; 1686 → 1264 → 948 → 711; 2472 → 1854 → 1390 → 1042 → 781). When y is odd the blocks are reshuffled and y grows (2361 → 5425, 781 → 2788).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 14,386 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
A 0 crawls through 1s at one cell per 5 steps, proved for every length.

sections.heading: Two blocks and a crawler
html: Stop the simulator whenever the head, in state A, steps onto a new cell at the right end. The tape is then, up to a few single marks, two long blocks of 1s with a gap 000 between them and a short tail:
The right end of the tape moves 2 cells at each of these moments, so the right side grows only as fast as these rounds come.

sections.heading: A 0 that crawls
html: Within a round, almost all the time is spent by a single 0 crawling through a block of 1s: C, B and A take turns, and every 5 steps the 0 has moved one cell to the right (proved in Lean for every length):

Inside a round a second 0 near the right end of the big block steps 3 cells to the left after each crawl (it sits 133, 130, 127, ... cells right of the start position), so the work of a round is proportional to the block; a full round moves about a quarter of the right block into the left one.

sections.heading: Three quarters, or a reshuffle
html: Write y for the right block. As long as y is ≡ 0 or 2 mod 4 the next round has y − ⌈y/4⌉, i.e. about 3y/4, and the left block takes the rest: 4198 → 3148 → 2361. When y is odd the round ends differently, the left block is cut down and y grows again (2361 → 5425, 781 → 2788). A rule that multiplies by 3/4 and branches on the residue mod 4 is of the same kind as the Collatz map; halting would come from a residue case at a small value that the regular rounds avoid, and nothing known rules it out or brings it about.
Status: the crawl is proved; the round and the odd case are read off the run (heuristic), not yet written as an exact map.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.535). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.124).
After 109 steps the tape spans 14,386 cells (11,274 left of the start, 155 right), with a density of 1s of 1.0.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

summary: Two big blocks of 1s and crawling 0s: each round a quarter of the right block moves over to the left one while the right block's length is even; an odd length triggers a different reshuffle. Collatz-like (factor 3/4, residues mod 4).
family: crawler moving quarters between two blocks (3/4 map)
